summary: Recommend explicit spawn-group ownership, latched cancellation and one lifecycle owner. This compacts the existing preflight; it adds no validation.

findings.claim: The runner conflates EOF/EAGAIN/EINTR and stops after direct-child exit plus two empty reads; cleanup kills only that PID without explicit reaping.
findings.recommendation: Track EOF only on read==0; retry EINTR and poll after EAGAIN. Close parent copies of child-side writers immediately after spawn. Fairly drain both pipes within limits. Clean up owned descendants even when their leader exited first or they closed their pipes.

findings.claim: Darwin spawn attributes establish group ownership before executable code runs; required APIs support a macOS 13 target.
findings.recommendation: Use absolute-path posix_spawn, SETPGROUP and pgroup=0, giving PGID=returned PID. Use CLOEXEC_DEFAULT with explicit /dev/null stdin and stdout/stderr dup2 actions. Use addchdir_np, available since macOS 10.15; the newer non-_np API is unsuitable for 13. Check all return codes, handle descriptor aliases, set intended signal masks/defaults, and avoid parent-side setpgid or global chdir.

findings.claim: Cancellation can occur before spawn; Swift still invokes the operation, and its cancellation handler can run concurrently. The current handler loses cancellation while Process is not running.
findings.recommendation: Maintain a locked cancellation latch and preparing/spawning/owned/finished states. onCancel only latches and wakes the owner. Check before spawn; publish successful PID while observing pending cancellation, then clean up immediately if cancelled. Never use a failed-spawn PID or resume continuations/cancel tasks under that lock.

findings.claim: TERM/KILL escalation needs retained PID/PGID ownership. Darwin WNOWAIT skips reaping, while WNOHANG may leave siginfo untouched.
findings.recommendation: One owner polls waitid(P_PID,pid,WEXITED|WNOHANG|WNOWAIT), zeroing si_pid each time. Retain the unreaped leader through the final group signal: this reuse-prevention inference requires exclusive reaping and no SIGCHLD auto-reap. Signal only -ownedPGID with PGID>1: TERM, finite grace, KILL, then targeted reap. Never signal after reap/ECHILD, use PID 0/-1, or enumerate unrelated PIDs. Report ownership/permission failures.

findings.claim: Foundation terminate promises SIGTERM to subtasks but no effect after receiver exit; it does not promise a retained group anchor. Group signalling cannot contain every descendant.
findings.recommendation: Use monotonic drain/termination/reap deadlines. SIGKILL does not guarantee finite-time reap: retain delayed cleanup in a capped exact-child reaper/admission slot and report incomplete cleanup. Descendants deliberately escaping via setsid/setpgid remain outside the guarantee; close local pipes at deadline. Regressions should cover pre-spawn cancellation, TERM resistance, leader-first exit, retained/closed descendant pipes, output caps, spawn failure and FD/zombie cleanup.
